limitations: Structural validity is not row acceptance; every row predicate is computed independently by the verifier.
A smoke run is diagnostic only and closes no row.
One 12-hour run on one host cannot prove indefinite bounded memory, every supported Kafka and Node pair, multi-host partitions or the compared consume benchmark.
The seeded control proves sensitivity to that seed only.
Performance results are report-only; no latency or throughput veto is created.

minFreeDiskBytes.source: design: post-cluster free disk covering the stream, telemetry, broker, archive, verifier and safety reservations

maxLoadAverage1m.source: design: quiet-host preflight floor, 0.25 per core on 12 cores

abortMemAvailableBytes.source: design: MemAvailable below this aborts the run non-green

maxStreamBytes.source: design: raw stream cap; overflow fails collection, rows are never dropped

maxEventLineBytes.source: design: ordinary record line cap, enforced on every record

maxTelemetryBytes.source: design: combined raw and decoded telemetry reservation

brokerReporterFileBytes.source: design: per-node telemetry reporter file cap, zero drops required

valueBytes.source: design: every offered value is exactly this long

maxOffers.source: design: total offers cap including probes and aborted records

mainRate.source: design: idempotent main offers per active second

telemetryProducerRate.source: design: telemetry producer main offers per active second

transactionEveryMs.source: design: one transaction per 100 active seconds, never overlapping

abortEvery.source: design: every tenth transaction is explicitly aborted

commitEvery.source: design: explicit commit at least once per this many processed records and at every drain

metadataMaxAgeMs.source: design: discovery clients refresh metadata within an auxiliary slot

telemetryPushMaxMs.source: design: declared telemetry push interval ceiling

visiblePerProducerKind.source: design: visible acknowledged records per producing kind; the scarcest kinds offer 12 x 3000 s x 0.2 = 7 200 telemetry records and 360 x 20 x 9 / 10 = 6 480 visible transaction records in 12 hours

mainPerGroup.source: design: distinct main ids processed by every ordinary group and accepted by share

transactionsPerGroup.source: design: visible transaction ids processed by every ordinary group; 360 transactions of 20 records in 12 hours, one in ten aborted, leave 6 480

auxiliaryPerIncarnation.source: design: probe ids per auxiliary topic incarnation

distinctOffsets.source: design: distinct main offsets entered per measured process inside its quiet-bounded interval; 11 x 50 x 60 x 20 = 660 000 potential offsets leave the same headroom as 1 000 000 of 1 380 000 did over 23 intervals

topology.routeRule: The verifier expands this table over the actual topic ids and partitions into every required (group, topic id, partition) route. A route starts at offset 0 on an empty log and seals only after producer closure, a terminal scan to the settled high watermark, handler drain and final broker commit or share acceptance; no route may start above the corpus, omit a partition, incarnation or static group, or end early.

jitterMs.source: design: periodic admission jitter around each slot target

periodicSlots.source: design: slots k = 0..1440 over the 43 200 000 ms acceptance run at the sample period

quietReadings.source: design: three matched quiet readings per idle boundary

interning-seeded.retains: Map<partition:offset, offset string> of every offset the seed's handler enters
interning-seeded.exemption: Excluded only from unseeded heap growth tests; still owes sampling, identity, resources, map clear and natural exit.

durable-loss.name: lost, substituted or duplicated durable records and unauthorized stale work

connected-report-only.source: rule: connected consumers legitimately hold long-poll requests, heartbeats and telemetry timers; no calibrated connected-idle ceiling exists

rules: The supplied expected tree sha, profile and matrix and the permitted config match the available archived bytes; the archived driver and schema modules match the expected candidate; digests, counts and per-source sequences are complete.

requestedMs is the mode length and runEndAt - runStartAt equals it; every readiness precedes runStartAt; the last natural exit lies within the teardown allowance after runEndAt; no subject process or client is substituted.
Each persistent process has its baseline, exactly one periodic sample per slot, its final sample and its exit; each subject process and the seed have readings 0, 1 and 2 at every quiet boundary.
Each idle window lasts at least 600 000 ms with zero offers, mutations and member changes while standing clients stay connected and running.

Every scheduled execution has, per applicable kind and client, its actual call arguments joined to the accepted subscription, before and after inventory, partition transfer, pause behaviour and delivery; names and aggregate shape counters never prove work; a regex topic created and deleted before a required client accepts it fails that client's execution.
Events and causes lie inside their execution in causal order; a terminal route drain may follow only within its recorded seal barrier.
Every producer, group, transaction and telemetry floor of the mode holds: traffic floors in acceptance, schedule smoke floors in smoke; a smoke run closes no row.

Each actual telemetry client, the producer and the consumer separately, has a startup proof, at least one decoded push with metrics > 0 in every idle window and at least one after every broker recovery, keyed by its own client instance and subscription ids; its declared push interval is at most telemetryPushMaxMs and the telemetry selection does not change during the run.
After every broker recovery each actual kind supplies its own recovery witness before that outage execution ends.

recovery.classic-eager-dynamic: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record
recovery.classic-eager-static: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record
recovery.classic-cooperative-dynamic: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record
recovery.classic-cooperative-static: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record
recovery.consumer-dynamic: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record
recovery.consumer-static: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record
recovery.share: a new raw acquisition and its accepted settlement response, both after the broker ready record
recovery.producer-idempotent: an acknowledged offer sent after the broker ready record
recovery.producer-transactional: a committed transaction begun after the broker ready record
recovery.admin: a successful metadata call begun after the broker ready record
recovery.telemetry-producer: an acknowledged offer and its own decoded push with metrics > 0, both after the broker ready record
recovery.telemetry-consumer: a processed handler-enter and its paired successful broker commit readback, both after the broker ready record, and its own decoded push with metrics > 0

rules: O = offered ids, each with exactly one final ack outcome; L = the independent final read_committed log, unique by (topic id, partition, offset); every L id is in O with equal key, value, headers and transaction and appears at most once; the application never resends an id.

Rejected or confirmed-aborted ids are absent from L; acknowledged or confirmed-committed ids appear exactly once; unknown produce ids appear at most once; an unknown transaction decision is non-green, never guessed.
Expected routes are the topology table expanded over actual topic ids and partitions, independent of the journal; journal routes equal them, start at 0 and seal at the raw terminal scan.

For every expected group and key, E = visible L in [route.from, route.to): E is non-empty for each data-bearing role and incarnation and meets its floor; every E record has an authorized handler with a processed outcome; every handler matches an expected route and an actual L location and payload; ordinary groups reach route.to with a non-null terminal broker next; share accepts every E record.

Commits are serialized per (group, key); every successful commit write or end, intermediate as well as final, is paired with a later successful broker readback of equal next before any other commit or reset of that key supersedes it; an unknown outcome needs readback reconciliation, never fabricated success or stale local publication.

processedPrefix(group, key, cut) walks scanned visible data offsets from route.from with successful authorized processing by cut; scan-proven control and aborted gaps may be crossed, unprocessed visible data may not; every committed next <= that prefix; no integer contiguity is assumed.

Before an old topic id is deleted: every offer outcome resolved, an independent terminal scan, every expected group drained with its final paired commit or share acceptance, then the delete confirmation; the same name and offset under a new topic id is a different identity.
A missing or wrong scan makes delivery non-green even when every observed handler matches an offer.

Authority intervals are half-open per (group, key, client): they open at a successful acquire and close at revoke-end, lost, incarnation invalidation or disconnect; at most one valid ordinary owner holds a key at any instant; revoke-begin closes nothing, so final pre-revoke progress and commits stay valid.

A handler-enter carries the original captured authority owning that exact key at entry; a commit begin and write carry an authority still valid at the actual write; a local publication needs the captured run, token, key and incarnation still eligible; a local epoch or token alone never grants another partition.
A new handler entry, commit write or publication after its interval closes fails; an old callback may still finish as stale afterwards, without a new write or publication.

A request transmitted before loss may complete unknown or refused afterwards: its possible remote outcome is recorded, any stale retry, write or cache publication is forbidden, and the broker is reconciled before replacement progress.
Same-owner replay is allowed only after a handler-end with outcome retry, with no successful processing or commit past it, and only for that same record next.

New-owner rebalance or outage replay is limited to [last confirmed broker next, old processed next) on the same topic id and key; records beyond are first deliveries; replay below a confirmed commit is unauthorized, as the main workload declares no intentional reset.

Allowed replay intervals derive independently from boundary, handler and readback causes; a replay record never authorizes itself; a duplicate durable append is distinct from a permitted consumer replay.

Share acquisitions are record locks, not partition ownership: a share handler offset lies inside an actual successful acquired range with matching client, group and delivery count, and several members fetching one partition is not an ownership violation.

Share redelivery needs a successful release, a decoded lock loss or an expiry consistent with the configured lock duration, then a new raw acquisition with a strictly greater delivery count; an accepted or rejected terminal settlement ends processing of that record; a request alone or a late terminal result never authorizes replay; timing ambiguity near expiry without wire evidence is INCONCLUSIVE.
Connected quiet is not zero: periodic and quiet pending and inflight requests, sockets, timers and resources are reported, and live Fetch, ShareFetch, heartbeat and telemetry work is legitimate.

All queue and request counts reconcile and their original owners stay observable; every raw resource, listener and socket id has an actual owner or a declared baseline harness scope; no retired run or client admits new work.

Persistent emitter and event registrations equal the baseline owner registrations plus those independently observed for currently live operations; a replacement socket or queue has its own creation baseline; transient listeners have live call scopes; a new unexplained event name or duplicate registration fails even when totals match.

A closed cohort, within the socket grace after disconnect, has empty original queues, destroyed sockets, no product timers and restored owned registrations; standing peers are excluded from this zero.

After all disconnects: queue pending and inflight 0, ledger cells and tickets 0, reset debts 0, share sessions, held records, ranges and cohorts 0, created minus destroyed sockets 0, TCPSocketWrap and Timeout equal the preconstruction baseline, and no unknown surviving type or id remains.
Every process and the supervisor exit with code 0 and no signal, naturally observed; the observer never destroys or unrefs product handles.

Only the 12 unseeded subject processes are judged; for process p and h = 0..11, Y[h] = the judged bytes of the V8 heap snapshot p writes after the last quiet reading of boundary h, the self bytes of every snapshot node except those of node type code (compiled code, bytecode and their bookkeeping), whoever owns them; X[h] = the minute the snapshot began.
endpoint = median(Y[9..11]) - median(Y[0..2]); slope = the least-squares slope of Y over X; HeapOK(p) iff endpoint <= the heap endpoint bound and slope <= the heap slope bound.
Medians of an even count take the upper middle.

A boundary without a usable snapshot leaves HeapOK(p) INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS. Every judged Y[h] is re-derived from its own sealed snapshot file (the process's file of boundary h, with the size the worker recorded); a summary record its file does not confirm leaves HeapOK(p) INCONCLUSIVE.

The seed writes the same snapshots and its endpoint is computed the same way; it is the positive control of the snapshot pipeline: unless it exceeds the seed's breach bound, HeapOK is INCONCLUSIVE for every process, and the seed never fails an unseeded process.
The whole-process heapUsed endpoint and slope of the quiet readings, the judged heap of the reader and the decoder, RSS, external memory and decreases are reported, never gated.

Accepted subscription and topic-id lifetimes are reconstructed from actual publication and invalidation, and keyed pause and resume arguments are replayed independently; checks run at every quiet boundary and immediately after every accepted retirement.

Every pause-state, including empty, resumed-only and pauseAll entries, keeps its first observed origin and last operation, and its (client, run, topic, origin topic id, subscription life) stays accepted and live; pauseAll, paused and resumed equal the replay; unassignment does not end an accepted lifetime.
Retired state ids are absent, never relabelled to a new topic id; assigned paused keys admit no new handler until resume; reassignment within one accepted lifetime keeps pause intent.
Every actual backing key of each table has the permitted live owner its table rule names; cardinalities come from enumerated keys and no byte-size bound is invented.

subscription.owner: accepted names follow actual publication and invalidation; desired names may differ only until publication and never at quiet; observed topic ids are the currently selected names, and an unknown topic id is missing proof, never a guessed incarnation

pause-state.owner: its client's accepted (topic, origin topic id, subscription life), which unassignment does not end; retired with that accepted lifetime

assignment.owner: the current assignment with an open authority interval; gone once revoke-end or lost closes it

membership-state.owner: the current token, plus an old token only while its holders count actual outstanding operations or tickets; a current empty token may remain, previous idle generations may not

operation-cell.owner: the exact union and multiplicity of live ticket name and partition keys; each ticket keeps its own topic id, never restamped to the latest incarnation; empty once every ticket ends

reset-debt.owner: the client's accepted or desired topic id; may survive unassignment and partial discharge; cleared on disconnect

topic-configurations.owner: the accepted subscription at stable cuts; a pending transition may explain desired names only until publication and never at quiet

preferred-replicas.owner: assigned keys at stable cuts; an empty topic entry right after invalidation is legitimate until the assignment prune

grown-topic-names.owner: current coordinator target and resolved names plus literals, never historical names

queued-seeks.owner: assigned keys at stable cuts; a transient old seek needs a still-live token or ticket and retires when its operation ends

cluster-targets.owner: the accepted or desired subscription and actual live resolution obligations

acquired.owner: assigned keys at stable cuts; a transient old entry needs a still-live token or ticket and retires when its operation ends

halted.owner: assigned keys at stable cuts; cleared with their assignment

share-state.owner: current nodes and workers, or raw unsettled acquisitions; idle sessions remain legitimate, detached sessions and settled records do not

rows.obligation: Soak harness records listener, socket, queue and handle counts and retained-heap trend after warm-up and GC, with a clean exit and no forced termination; idle, regex-topic churn, member churn and outage/recovery runs; repeated producer and consumer churn gates; the final long-run evidence or an explicit reviewed replacement for the 24-hour commitment (a short churn loop cannot count as that run); evidence as JSONL.

scope.judged: all 12 unseeded subject processes; the seed only for sensitivity

rows.predicate: run PASS iff Complete, Delivery, AuthorityOK, ResourcesOK and TablesOK hold, HeapOK holds for each of the 12 unseeded subject processes and the offset-retention sensitivity of rs-l16 is conclusive. closure COMPLETE only with verified prior-checkpoint dispositions and every required companion.

minima.name: subject and seed quiet readings (13 x 36)

rows.fail: One static group's routes, handlers and commits are removed while its labels stay.
rows.pass: A complete run with legal at-least-once replay, invisible aborted transactions, connected idle long polls and a separately breaching seed.

rows.obligation: Harness with retained-heap assertions, repeated producer and consumer churn gates and the final long run, or a reviewed replacement.

scope.judged: each of the 12 unseeded subject processes on its own series; seed and observer series never substitute

rows.predicate: PASS iff Complete's time, sample and topology checks hold, every required subject slot has its own standing process, each has 12 post-warm-up matched quiet triplets with two new forced collections per reading, and every subject passes HeapOK on its own series. Full closure keeps the repeated-gate receipts.

minima.name: quiet readings per subject process (12 x 3)
forced collections for subject quiet readings

rows.fail: The admin process has only active samples, or the seed series is used as consumer-dynamic's series.
rows.pass: Each subject plateaus within +1.5 MiB with a permissible signed slope while the seed grows above 2 MiB; a pass means the screen passed, not indefinite boundedness.

rows.obligation: Soak harness asserting listener, socket, queue and handle counts with clean exit and no forced termination; idle, regex-topic churn, member churn and outage/recovery runs; evidence as JSONL.

scope.judged: every persistent process and client, connected idle distinct from closed and final

rows.predicate: PASS iff the relevant Complete schedule and grid hold and ResourcesOK holds for every persistent process and client. Connected aggregate totals are reported, not forced to 0 or equality.
rows.fail: A detached extra's request or timer survives closure while a standing member still polls.
rows.pass: A standing idle Fetch in flight plus legitimate heartbeat and telemetry timers; every retired owner clears, the final baseline is restored and every process exits naturally.

rows.obligation: Suite exits without forceExit; --detectOpenHandles clean; original teardown error absent or root-caused.

scope.judged: the three static kinds and their extras, plus the exact-candidate natural-exit suite companion

rows.predicate: run PASS iff each static kind has >= 12 real restart pairs with the same static id, a new actual client id and no concurrent duplicate static id, each followed by actual assignment, handler and broker commit; ResourcesOK holds for every cohort and process; disconnect < final sample < parent-observed exit. closure COMPLETE iff run PASS and the natural-exit companion is valid for the exact candidate: run attempt, Node 22, 24 and 26 coverage, ordinary, static, classic and consumer test identities, enforced open-handle detection, original teardown logs absent or root-caused, and a seeded retained timer or socket failing its watchdog.
rows.fail: Worker exit 0 with a missing, wrong-candidate or force-exited suite receipt.
rows.pass: The broker retains the static slot during a same-id restart, resources ultimately close and the suite receipt is valid.

rows.obligation: Longer run or histogram with enough samples; denominators pre-declared; tolerance not widened. Actual delivery-gap samples.

scope.judged: four consuming kinds, each paired with the idempotent producer on main

rows.predicate: For each of the four consuming kinds: latency[i] = first authorized handler-enter at in its group for main id i minus the idempotent offered at; require >= 20 000 distinct ids and no negative latency. Gaps are consecutive actual handler-entry time differences on one client and run within one active phase and owner episode; cross-idle and boundary gaps are excluded and counted; require >= 20 000 actual gaps, so >= 20 001 eligible entries. Report entry counts, exclusions, histograms and p50/p90/p99 with percentile(p) = sorted[ceil(p*n)-1], never as a veto.
rows.fail: One group supplies all 80 000 samples, or 20 000 entries are counted as 20 000 gaps.
rows.pass: First-handler latency once per id, replay identified separately, actual gap floors met; a slow p99 is reported without an invented threshold.

rows.obligation: Retained-heap result in the consume benchmark that fails when the interning returns.

scope.judged: the unseeded eager-dynamic, consumer-dynamic and share processes and the isolated seed, on main

rows.predicate: For p in {eager-dynamic, consumer-dynamic, share, seed}: V[p] = distinct main offsets actually entered in p between its first quiet triplet completion and its last quiet triplet admission; require |V[p]| >= 475 000 from the same main corpus and method. The seed's judged-heap endpoint, from its own snapshots as in HeapOK, must exceed the breach bound; every unseeded process passes HeapOK. A missing, under-volume or under-bound seed is INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS; a seed breach never fails an unseeded memory row. closure COMPLETE also needs the consume-retention companion with the candidate and reference retained and control report; otherwise the row stays OPEN.
rows.fail: A million callbacks on one offset; distincts only before baseline; the right seed name in the wrong process; healthy subjects with a blind seed.
rows.pass: Healthy subjects, exact interval volume, an isolated breaching seed through its last quiet reading, then clear and natural exit.

rows.obligation: Harness, then the consumer churn gate (regex topic churn, pause/resume, recreation) asserts bounded paused and generation set sizes, then the final long run.

scope.judged: regex on eager-dynamic, cooperative-dynamic, cooperative-static and consumer-dynamic; pause and recreation on all six ordinary kinds

rows.predicate: PASS iff the applicable Complete executions hold and TablesOK holds for every ordinary kind. Each regex execution accepts the add and the retire on each required client; each recreation retires the old intent and witnesses a distinct new one.

minima.name: regex accepted add and retire pairs (48 x 4)
quiet readings of regex processes (4 x 36)

rows.fail: Old-incarnation state persists after the new incarnation is accepted, even empty or resumed-only; a removed client subscription saved by another member's live route; an equal-size stale replacement.
rows.pass: A paused unassigned partition within one accepted lifetime survives and reapplies; true retirement removes it; a new pause on the new incarnation gets a new origin and state identity.

rows.obligation: Retained-heap trend after warm-up and GC across cooperative rounds measured by the harness and the churn gates; slope and cause established or recorded as bounded; final long run.

scope.judged: the cooperative-dynamic and cooperative-static processes, each independently

rows.predicate: For each cooperative kind: R = distinct successful (group, run, round) inside its membership executions with negotiated cooperative protocol and corroborated partition transfer; require >= 1 such round in each of the 48 executions and >= 48 in total; its process passes HeapOK, TablesOK and AuthorityOK. PASS iff both kinds satisfy this independently and the quiet grid is complete. A positive slope within the screen prints 'positive within declared screen; long-run boundedness not proven'.
rows.fail: Both names present but only eager members acted, or equal-count stale cooperative keys.
rows.pass: Actual cooperative transfers, proper lifetimes including legitimate unassigned pause, a screen-bounded plateau and natural exit.
